nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a unitary s-Zumkeller number and let $q$ be the least unitary divisor of $n$ greater than $1$. If $q = 2$, then $n$ has more than $2^6$ unitary divisors; if $q = 3$ or $q = 4$, then $n$ has more than $2^2$ unitary divisors.
nodes.title: Unitary divisor counts of unitary s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: A positive integer $n$ with $m$ distinct prime factors has exactly $2^m$ unitary divisors.
nodes.title: Number of unitary divisors

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, let $T(n)$ be the product of the positive divisors of $n$ and $\tau(n)$ their number. Then $T(n)^2 = n^{\tau(n)}$.
nodes.title: Square of the product of the divisors

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $T(n)$ is the product of all positive divisors of $n$. For $n = 0$ the set of divisors is taken to be empty, so $T(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: Product of the divisors

nodes.summary: Every odd s-Zumkeller number divisible by $3$ has at least $8$ distinct prime factors.
nodes.title: Odd s-Zumkeller numbers divisible by $3$ have at least eight prime factors

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be an even s-Zumkeller number and let $\tau(n)$ be the number of positive divisors of $n$. Then $\tau(n) / \sum_{d \mid n} d^{-2} \le 2\tau(n)/3$, where the sum runs over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$.
nodes.title: Harmonic mean of squared divisors of even s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \ge 1$ be an integer, let $n = 2^\alpha (2^{\alpha+1} - 1)$ and let $\tau(n)$ be the number of positive divisors of $n$. If $n$ is s-Zumkeller, then $\tau(n) / \sum_{d \mid n} d^{-2} < 2^{2\alpha+3}/3$, where the sum runs over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$.
nodes.title: Harmonic mean of squared divisors of s-Zumkeller numbers $2^\alpha(2^{\alpha+1}-1)$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $n$ is $k$-m-perfect if $T(n) = n^k$, where $T(n)$ is the product of the divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: $k$-m-perfect numbers

nodes.summary: Every odd s-Zumkeller number is a perfect square.
nodes.title: Odd s-Zumkeller numbers are perfect squares

nodes.summary: The number $4$ is super-m-Zumkeller, and for no natural number $k \ge 2$ is $4$ a $k$-m-perfect number. This is the paper's counterexample to the converse of Theorem 6.
nodes.title: $4$ is super-m-Zumkeller but not $k$-m-perfect for $k \ge 2$

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, let $\tau(n)$ be the number of positive divisors of $n$ and $T(n)$ their product. Then $n$ is super-m-Zumkeller if and only if $8$ divides $\alpha \cdot \tau(n) \cdot \tau(T(n))$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$, where $\alpha$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$.
nodes.title: Criterion for super-m-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number with $k \equiv 0 \pmod 4$. Then every natural number that is $k$-m-perfect is super-m-Zumkeller.
nodes.title: $k$-m-perfect numbers with $k$ a positive multiple of $4$ are super-m-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $\alpha \ge 1$ an integer. Then $p^\alpha$ is super-m-Zumkeller if and only if $\alpha \equiv 0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13$ or $15 \pmod{16}$.
nodes.title: Super-m-Zumkeller prime powers

nodes.summary: For every finite set $S$ of at least three primes, the product $\prod_{p \in S} p$ is super-m-Zumkeller.
nodes.title: Products of at least three distinct primes are super-m-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $S$ a finite set of at least three odd primes. Then $2^k \prod_{p \in S} p$ is super-m-Zumkeller.
nodes.title: Powers of $2$ times at least three distinct odd primes are super-m-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an odd natural number and let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes. Then $2^k p q$ is super-m-Zumkeller.
nodes.title: Odd powers of $2$ times two distinct odd primes are super-m-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $T(n)$ be the product of the positive divisors of $n$ (for $n = 0$ the divisor set is taken to be empty, so $T(0) = 1$). Then $n$ is *super-m-Zumkeller* if there is a set $A$ of positive divisors of $T(n)$ such that the product of the elements of $A$ equals the product of the positive divisors of $T(n)$ that are not in $A$; that is, the divisors of $T(n)$ split into two complementary…
nodes.title: Super-m-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be an even s-Zumkeller number and let $\sigma_2(n)$ be the sum of the squares of the positive divisors of $n$. Then $\sigma_2(n)$ is even, some odd prime $p$ divides $n$ with an odd exponent in the prime factorization of $n$, and $3n^2 \le 2\sigma_2(n)$.
nodes.title: Properties of even s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be an even positive integer and let $\sigma_2(n)$ be the sum of the squares of the positive divisors of $n$. Then $n$ is s-Zumkeller if and only if there is a (possibly empty) set $S$ of proper divisors of $n$, not containing $n/2$, such that $4 \sum_{d \in S} d^2 = 2\sigma_2(n) - 3n^2$.
nodes.title: Criterion for even s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: The number $60$ is s-Zumkeller: the squares of its proper divisors $1, 2, 5, 30$ sum to $1^2 + 2^2 + 5^2 + 30^2 = 930$, which is half of the sum of the squares of all proper divisors of $60$.
nodes.title: $60$ is s-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is s-Zumkeller if its proper divisors can be split into two disjoint nonempty sets whose elements have equal sums of squares. Each of the two sums is then $(\sigma_2(n) - n^2)/2$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a unitary s-Zumkeller number, let $q$ be the least unitary divisor of $n$ greater than $1$, and for each prime $p$ dividing $n$ let $k_p$ be the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Then, with both sums over all unitary divisors $d$ of $n$ (including $n$ itself), $n^2 (2/q^2 + 1) \le \sum_d d^2$ and $2/q^2 + 1 \le \sum_d 1/d^2$. nodes.title: Lower bounds for unitary s-Zumkeller numbers

nodes.summary: The number $60$ is a unitary s-Zumkeller number: its proper unitary divisors are $1, 3, 4, 5, 12, 15, 20$, and $20^2 + 3^2 + 1^2 = 410$ is half the sum of their squares.
nodes.title: The number 60 is unitary s-Zumkeller

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is a unitary s-Zumkeller number when its proper unitary divisors (the unitary divisors of $n$ other than $n$) split into two nonempty disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ with equal sums of squares, $\sum_{d \in A} d^2 = \sum_{d \in B} d^2$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
